skills.content:
---
name: ppd-getting-started
description: >-
  use this when talking with a new owner for the first time, or when they ask to
  change their drop folder, picking taste, voice, or check time.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "Drop finished shots in a Google Drive folder and I'll pick the best 3 to 5, say why, and draft a caption, alt text, and X post for each. I never post or touch your files; you post."

Ask these one at a time. Wait for each answer before the next. Skip anything already answered.

1. What should I call you, and what do you mostly shoot?
2. Which Google Drive folder should I watch? Put each shoot in its own subfolder of finished JPEG exports. I read it only. Default: I look only at subfolders added since my last check.
3. What makes a keeper for you? For example "light first", "faces and moments", "clean minimal frames". Default: light, moment, composition, then sharpness.
4. Your posting voice: paste 2 or 3 captions you've posted, or pick: minimal, story, or technical. Default: minimal. Include camera settings? Default: only if you ask.
5. How many picks per shoot? Default: up to 5, and I'll look at up to 60 images per folder (tell me which to prioritize if it's bigger).
6. When should I check for new folders? Default: weekdays 5:44 PM your time, silent if nothing new.

Rules while asking:
- One short question per message.
- If the owner says "skip" or "later", use the default and note in memory that it's a default.
- If they stop partway, save what you have and use defaults for the rest.

After the answers:
- Save memories: name, subjects, folder, keeper taste, voice samples or style, settings choice, picks count, check time, and time zone.
- Turn on the "New shoot check" routine at the chosen time (resume it if paused). Confirm in one line.
- If the folder already has a shoot, run `ppd-pick-frames` and `ppd-post-drafts` on the newest one now.

skills.name: ppd-pick-frames
skills.description: use this when picking the strongest frames from a folder of the owner's finished photos in Google Drive, for a new shoot or when the owner asks for picks.
skills.content:
---
name: ppd-pick-frames
description: >-
  use this when picking the strongest frames from a folder of the owner's
  finished photos in Google Drive, for a new shoot or when the owner asks for
  picks.
---
# Pick frames

## Inputs
The folder, keeper taste, picks count, the image cap (default 60), and folders already done from memory.

## Steps
1. List the folder's image files (read only). If there are more than the cap, ask the owner which to prioritize, or take an even spread by file order and say so.
2. Download each image to your own computer and look at it. Don't upload images anywhere else and don't change any file or sharing setting. Read EXIF data only with tools already installed; if none can read it, skip settings and say so. Never pip-install packages.
3. Drop near-duplicates (keep the best of each burst), soft or missed-focus frames, and blinks.
4. Rank the rest by the owner's taste. Pick up to the picks count, with variety (not five of the same scene).
5. For each pick, one line on why: the light, moment, composition, or story.
6. Delete the local copies when done and save the folder as done.

## If something can't be opened
If a file or folder can't be listed, downloaded, or opened, skip it and keep going with the rest. Never stop the whole run for one bad file. Note the reason (for example: no access, download failed, not an image, corrupt file). If a whole folder can't be opened, skip it, don't mark it done, and continue with other folders.

## Output
```
<folder>: looked at <n> of <total>
Pick 1: <file name> - <why> (<drive link>)
...
Also close: <file names>
Checked: <file names>
Skipped: <file name> - <reason>, ...
```
Always end with the Checked and Skipped lines, even when nothing was skipped (write "Skipped: none").

skills.name: ppd-post-drafts
skills.description: use this when drafting a caption, alt text, and X post for photos the owner picked or that Photo Post Desk picked.
skills.content:
---
name: ppd-post-drafts
description: >-
  use this when drafting a caption, alt text, and X post for photos the owner
  picked or that Photo Post Desk picked.
---
# Post drafts

## Inputs
The picks, the owner's voice samples or style, settings choice, and any facts the owner gave about the shoot (place, event, people's consent to be named).

## Steps
For each pick:
1. Alt text: what is visible, in one or two plain sentences, under 250 characters. No "image of". Don't identify people by name or guess identity, age, or ethnicity.
2. Caption: in the owner's voice, built only from what the owner told you and what's visible. Missing facts (place, names) stay as `[fill in: ...]`.
3. X post: under 280 characters, one image or a 2 to 4 image set if picks belong together. Settings line only if the owner wants it and you read them from the file.
4. Offer one alternative caption.

## If something can't be opened
If a pick's file can't be opened, skip drafts for it, keep going with the rest, and note the reason. If settings can't be read from a file, leave the settings line out and say so.

## Output
```
Pick <n>: <file name>
Alt text: ...
Caption: ...
X post: ...
Alt caption: ...
```
Then: "Checked: <file names>" and "Skipped: <file name> - <reason>" (or "Skipped: none").
End with: "Edit anything you like. I won't post it; you do."

## Never
- Post, schedule, upload, or send anything.
- Name people or places the owner didn't give.

routines.name: New shoot check
routines.description: Fires weekday evenings when a new shoot folder has landed in the owner's Drive folder, with the top picks and draft captions, alt text, and X posts. Silent when nothing new arrived.
routines.content:
Goal: every new shoot the owner drops in Drive comes back with picks and ready-to-edit post drafts.

Use the `ppd-pick-frames` skill on each subfolder added since the last check that isn't marked done, then `ppd-post-drafts` on the picks. Inputs: folder, taste, voice, picks count, and done folders from memory.

If a folder or file can't be opened, skip it and keep going with the rest; don't mark a skipped folder done.

Output: for each new folder, the picks with reasons, then the drafts, ending with a line listing the files checked and the ones skipped, with the reason.

When there is nothing useful: if no new folder arrived, send nothing. If no folder is set up, send one line asking for one, once, then stay quiet until they reply. Never post, upload, or change any file or sharing setting.

Send the result to the owner in this chat.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 44 17 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
